podcast.body: Released in 1953, "Hound Dog" appeared on the flip side of the single "Don't Be Cruel." Both songs were significant hits for Elvis Presley, contributing to his extensive catalog of double A-side successes. "Elvis Presley's Houndog was on the other side of Don't Be Cruel back in 1953."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Digital Debris Part 1: B-Sides and Bonus Tracks

podcast.body: A cover version of Big Mama Thornton's song, chosen by Elvis for what would become his biggest double-sided hit, though it bore almost no relation to Thornton's original. It took 31 takes to record and, combined with "Don't Be Cruel," spent 11 weeks at the top of the charts, reaching number 2 before swapping with "Don't Be Cruel" to hit number 1. "These days, their cover version of Big Mama Thunton's Hound Dog is the better known of the two sides they cut that day, but while that's an excellent track, and one that bears almost no relation to Thunton's original."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: A major hit for Elvis Presley in 1956, "Hound Dog" was one of the prominent rock and roll songs of the year, though its worldwide chart positions were ultimately surpassed by Fats Domino's "Blueberry Hill." "Worldwide, Blueberry Hill was the biggest rock and roll hit of 1956, outdoing even Elvis's Hound Dog and Hard Break Hotel in Worldwide Chart positions."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
